table_title: For each continent, list the major international transboundary rivers that are at least 1000 kilometers long, including a boundary-aware continent label and the countries they traverse.
db_analog: SELECT continent_labels, river, length_km, countries FROM major_international_transboundary_rivers WHERE length_km >= 1000 ORDER BY continent_labels, river
temporal_note: Wikipedia pages accessed in 2026. Core coverage comes from the Wikipedia "Transboundary river" page section "List of major international transboundary rivers", filtered to rows with length at least 1000 km (20 rows; Ichamati, Meuse, Rhône, and St. Lawrence fall below the threshold and are excluded). This is a partially_supplemented instance: 13 additional major international transboundary rivers of >=1000 km were added one-by-one from their own dedicated Wikipedia pages (each verified for length >=1000 km and >=2 countries) to fill omissions from the self-declared "major" list, covering Africa, Asia, South America, the Europe/Asia boundary, and Oceania (Fly and Sepik). The 33-row count reflects this curated major-river set and is not a globally exhaustive per-continent inventory.
_extraction_notes: claim_type = partially_supplemented (recorded authoritatively in curation.json). Derived from the staged >100 miles version by raising the threshold to >=1000 km. The universe is Wikipedia's "Transboundary river" page section "List of major international transboundary rivers" (a self-declared *major* list, not exhaustive): 20 of its 24 rows are >=1000 km and retained; Ichamati (334), Meuse (925), Rhône (813), and St. Lawrence (500) fall below the threshold and are removed. Because the list is explicitly only "major", 13 further major international transboundary rivers of >=1000 km were supplemented one-by-one, each from its own dedicated Wikipedia page and each confirmed to be >1000 km AND transboundary (>=2 countries): Senegal, Ubangi, Orange, Amur, Salween, Ili, Paraná, Paraguay, Uruguay, Madeira, Ural, Fly, and Sepik. See curation.json::proposed_supplements for the per-river audit trail. The schema uses a boundary-aware `Continent(s)` field, so Ural is represented as `Europe; Asia` rather than being forced into a single continent bucket. This is a curated, non-exhaustive major-river set, not a globally complete per-continent inventory.
